Sprint 42: the goal
we committed to
Two demos, the numbers under the hood, and what we pull into sprint 43 and what we park.
Two demos on staging, against last week's real incidents. Slides only for what the terminal cannot show.
Open an incident and the timeline writes the first paragraph: what changed, when, and the first symptom.
Deploy at 14:02, latency alert at 14:09, narrative drafted at 14:09:30. The on-call reads instead of digging.
Overlapping deploys, missing traces, and a timeline with nothing in it all produce an honest sentence.

Eleven seconds
for ten thousand
traces.
Every first sentence needs ten thousand traces. The row store took eleven seconds to hand them over.
Eleven seconds is longer than the on-call waits before opening the dashboards anyway.
One table, no partitions, and every incident querying the same hot rows at once.
Traces now land in a columnar store partitioned by hour: two engineers, three weeks, one migration script. The old row store stays read-only until December.
Old row store still answers, read-only
What you just saw  ·  edge cases and the figure that moved
An incident with no traces attached
A timeline with nothing on it yet
on-call digging before a first summary
the on-call reads, then goes to the fix
Ten thousand traces under a second
Migration ran twice in staging, once in prod
Old row store still answers, read-only
ten thousand traces on the row store
the same query on the columnar store
figures from Tuesday's run, not a rehearsal
Third sprint in a row above the rolling average.
First clean sprint since June; the trace store tests paid off.
Down from eleven seconds on the old store.
Both waiting on the vendor contract for APAC.
one clean sprint is a good week, three is a trend

It wrote the paragraph I would have
written at minute twenty. I read it
at minute one and went to the fix.
On-call, platform team. Used the draft on Tuesday's 14:09 alert
the real alert, not a fixture

Demo recordings and the sprint report are in the channel. Retro on Monday at ten.
